description: The Climate Resilient City Tool, earlier called the Adaptation Support Tool (AST2.0), is a web tool for exploring climate adaptation measures in an urban area. Users select an area, draw blue-green and grey measures on a map against flooding, drought and urban heat, compare the measures' effectiveness and see how far a plan is from a pre-set target, such as a storage volume or heat reduction goal. It is designed for stakeholder workshops and can run on a touch table, with documentation built into the tool. It was first developed in the Climate-KIC Blue Green Dream project and further developed by Deltares, which maintains it with support from the Dutch government; it has been tested in Berlin, London, Paris and several Dutch cities. The tool is available online free of charge after accepting its terms and conditions, as a hosted web application. Caveats: effectiveness values are generic screening estimates, not local model results, and outputs need to be checked with detailed hydraulic or climate models. It supports early-stage climate adaptation planning of green and blue infrastructure that is later tested with models; a related record is the EPA National Stormwater Calculator.
licence: Free to use under the tool's terms and conditions
